clue.text: Appreciate reverse of online interconnection is not finishing school

indicators.note: the clue asks for the reverse of the term for the online interconnection, so read it backwards

parts.note: the web is the interconnected network of online pages
taken as written

indicators.note: not finishing tells us to cut the last letter off the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone appreciates that a web connection isn't the same as completing a finishing school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns WEB into BEW; 'not finishing' drops the final N of ETON to leave ETO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wise to something is to be aware of it, so it can stand for appreciate in the sense of realise.

clue.text: One of 24 comes by restricting currency

indicators.note: restricting means the word by holds the currency inside it, confining it

parts.note: taken as written
the rand is the South African unit of currency

explanation.surface: Something arrives because spending money has been rationed.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is DRINKS, so the definition asks for a drink. 'comes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an example of the drinks named at 24.

clue.text: One of 24 is getting £1,000, within reason

indicators.note: within says the next pieces sit inside the word for reason

parts.note: why means a reason, as in the whys and wherefores
taken as written
K (from kilo, a thousand) is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A drink that comes with a thousand-pound price tag, within reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a distilled spirit, one example of the drinks at 24.

clue.text: One of 24 to slip into cast

indicators.note: into says the slip is placed inside the word for cast

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy
to err is to make a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A drink that slips into a theatre company's cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Spain, one of the drinks at 24.

clue.text: Old buildings — I find the top of one in the Lakes

indicators.note: in places the run of letters inside the word for lakes

parts.note: tarns are small mountain lakes, as in the English Lake District
taken as written
taken as written
one of the old buildings: the top of a building is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: In the Lake District someone finds the roof of an old building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the top of one' refers back to the definition: one building, whose first letter is B. A tithe barn stored the tenth of produce owed to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithe barns were medieval farm buildings that held the tithes paid to the church, so they are old buildings.

clue.text: Boy servant entertaining animal without tail to awaken 2

indicators.note: entertaining means the servant hosts, or holds inside, the shortened animal

parts.note: a fag was a junior boy acting as a servant to an older pupil at an English public school

indicators.note: without tail says the animal loses its last letter

parts.note: a mouse is a small animal
to rouse is to awaken someone

explanation.surface: A schoolboy servant feeds a tailless pet to wake up with a dram.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is WHISKY, so the definition asks for a whisky brand. 'without tail' cuts the E from MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Famous Grouse is a well-known brand of blended Scotch, an instance of the drink at 2.

clue.text: Bill with one way out for pollutant

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
I is the Roman numeral for one
a drain is a way out for water

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill is offered as a way out of pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made acidic by industrial emissions, a form of environmental pollution.

clue.text: Outer door for pupil with gall

parts.note: at Oxford and Cambridge colleges the outer door of a student's rooms is called the oak
the pupil of the eye is called its apple

explanation.surface: A school pupil has the gall to stand at the outer door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gall' looks like cheek, but it is a growth on a plant. 'Sporting the oak' meant shutting your outer door at Oxbridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a round growth on oak trees caused by wasp larvae: a type of plant gall.

clue.text: Cross round a model village

indicators.note: round says the cross goes around the following letter

parts.note: a saltire is a diagonal cross, as on the Scottish flag

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about a model village.
explanation.walkthrough: Saltaire is a model village built by Titus Salt for mill workers near Bradford in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltaire is a planned Victorian industrial settlement, the classic British example of a model village.

clue.text: One of 24 with one group coming in before

indicators.note: coming in tells us the pieces enter the word for before

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room
I is the Roman numeral for one
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A drink is joined by a crowd who arrive early.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, so it belongs among the drinks of 24.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish coin

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone pockets a Spanish coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American and Canadian five-cent coin.

clue.text: Tip of England's country lake's in a Midland region

indicators.note: tip here is the far end of the word, so take its last letter

parts.note: UK is short for United Kingdom, a country
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes; with the possessive it becomes Erie's

explanation.surface: The tip of England has a lake in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a geographical point, but it is the final letter of 'England'. The Dukeries is a part of Sherwood Forest, Nottinghamshire, once home to four ducal estates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dukeries is a district of north Nottinghamshire, an area in the English Midlands.

clue.text: One of 24 and letters lost by ancestor

indicators.note: lost by says these letters are taken away from the word for the ancestor

parts.note: a grandpapa is a grandfather, an ancestor
the letters of the word and, removed in whatever order they are found

explanation.surface: A drink and some letters go missing from Grandad's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: One A, the N and the D of 'and' come out of GRANDPAPA, not as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace, one of the drinks at 24.

clue.text: Tiny blonde possibly responsible for the 5 5

indicators.note: possibly says the words could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A small fair-haired girl may be to blame for the Famous Five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 5 5' reads as the answer to 5 twice: FAMOUS, plus 5 as a number, i.e. the Famous Five.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid Blyton wrote the Famous Five children's adventure series, so she is responsible for them.

clue.text: Analgesic for father taking half 24 and getting less well

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the answer to 24 has six letters; its middle three form half of it, ink
iller means more ill, so less well

explanation.surface: Dad takes half his drinks and feels worse, so reaches for a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is DRINKS; INK is the half that sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a medicine that relieves pain, which is exactly what a painkiller does.

clue.text: One of 24 religious reformer's lost in troubles

indicators.note: lost tells us the word in drops out of the reformer's name

parts.note: John Calvin was the Protestant reformer of Geneva
ados are fusses or troubles

explanation.surface: A drink: a religious reformer gets lost in his troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the reformer inside troubles, but it is the piece that 'lost' removes. Calvados is the definition's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is an apple brandy from Normandy, one of the drinks of 24.

clue.text: One of 24 with support for arm under trap

indicators.note: under places the support below the trap in this down entry

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
a sling is a bandage that supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: A drink served with an arm in a sling beneath a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin sling is a cocktail of gin, sugar and water, one of the drinks of 24.

clue.text: Pirate boy in previous day across the water

indicators.note: in says the boy goes inside the foreign word for the previous day

parts.note: hier is French for yesterday, France being across the Channel
Jack is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pirate boy crossed the water yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijacker seizes a vehicle or ship by force, which is what a pirate does.

clue.text: Fan finds a fish, say, at island party

indicators.note: say tells us the letters are pronounced like the word fish in this answer

parts.note: the letters FIC are pronounced fish in the middle of this word
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A fan finds a fish at a party on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen enthusiast, which is another word for a fan.

clue.text: See 5
2 to nip in the bud?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 2 is a whisky
to ... a plan is to stop it before it develops

explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is both whisky distilled in Scotland and a verb meaning to put an end to something early.

clue.text: Ornate state nearly split £1 in passage

indicators.note: nearly says the state's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Florida is a US state

explanation.surface: An elaborate state shares a pound in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: A double wordplay: 'split £1 in passage' also gives the answer, L and I (from £1) separately splitting FORD, a passage over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid means elaborately decorated or flowery, a close synonym of ornate.

clue.text: Meat has trapped holy virgin

indicators.note: has trapped means the meat holds the next letters inside

parts.note: veal is calf meat
ST stands for saint, a holy person

explanation.surface: A piece of meat has caught a holy virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holy virgin' looks like one phrase, but 'holy' gives ST and 'virgin' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vestal was one of the Roman priestesses sworn to chastity, so the word means a virgin.

clue.text: Wrong call catches boy in a sort of error

indicators.note: catches means the rearranged letters hold the boy inside
wrong indicates the next word is put into a wrong order

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Making a bad phone call catches a boy out in a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong call' reads as a mistaken phone call, but 'Wrong' is the anagram signal on 'call', giving CLAL; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerical error is a slip in copying or writing, a kind of mistake.

clue.text: Writers on doctor's round?

indicators.note: on places the writers after the doctor in this across entry

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
inks are what writers use; cryptically, things that write

explanation.surface: Authors accompany a doctor on his rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a medical round, but is a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is the set of drinks bought for everyone in a group at a pub.

clue.text: Street with composer who does his stuff?

parts.note: John Rutter is an English composer of choral music

explanation.surface: A composer on the street performs his routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A strutter is someone who struts, and the idiom is to strut your stuff, showing off.

clue.text: Setter (female) in fine unable to escape?

the setter refers to themself as me
she is the female pronoun

explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshed means caught as in a net, so trapped and unable to get free.
